newsitem.title: FINLAND: FINANCE MINISTRY OUTLINES FUND TO SHIELD INVESTORS.
newsitem.headline: FINANCE MINISTRY OUTLINES FUND TO SHIELD INVESTORS.

text.p: A finance ministry committee said on Friday that Finland should establish a fund to protect small investors from mishandling by financial service firms and credit institutions.
"The existence of a compensation fund would improve the legal status of the small investor," the finance ministry said in a statement.

The committee proposed that investment service firms and credit institutions would be required to join a compensation fund to cover investors' losses up to 116,000 markka in case mishandling is found in insolvent firms, the ministry said.
It would not cover losses associated with investment risk, the ministry said. Institutional and professional investors would not be covered by the fund, it said.
Many European countries already have such compensation schemes, and the European Union is drafting a directive which would require Finland to establish one by the end of 1998, the ministry said.
The fund initially collect 50 million markka from financial services firms and credit institutions during a five-year transition period, it said.
